title: Signature Privacy Budget Ledger
description: Signature edition: every epsilon spent is journaled — who queried, what, when, the remaining budget — in a tamper-evident ledger. Privacy spend becomes auditable like financial spend; exceeding budget requires the same ceremony as overspending money. This is a Signature original method.
method: Journal each query's spend with (analyst, query hash, ε, remaining); alert on unusual spend; require approval past thresholds.
usage: Review the ledger like expenses; investigate anomalous query patterns.

demo.code:
print('ledger: analyst chen, query #8812, eps 0.2, remaining 3.1')
print('unusual: 10 queries in 1h -> approval required')

title: Signature Gaussian mechanism
description: Signature edition: For (ε,δ)-differential privacy, Gaussian noise often beats Laplace on utility — especially for high-dimensional queries like gradient updates in DP-SGD. The noise scales with sensitivity times √(log(1/δ))/ε; δ is the tiny probability the guarantee bends.
method: Calibrate σ ≥ Δ₂√(2ln(1.25/δ))/ε; add N(0,σ²); track (ε,δ) composition.
usage: Use for ML training and vector queries; keep δ cryptographically small (≪ 1/n).

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(7)
true_mean, sigma = 5.0, 0.8
print(f'true mean 5.0 -> released {random.gauss(true_mean, sigma):.2f} (Gaussian, sigma=0.8)')

title: Signature Synthetic data with DP
description: Signature edition: Instead of answering queries, generate a synthetic dataset with DP guarantees (via DP-GANs, MST, or marginal-based methods) and let analysts query it freely. The synthetic data preserves statistical patterns while no synthetic row corresponds to a real person — privacy once, utility many times.
method: Learn DP-noisy marginals or train a DP generative model; sample synthetic rows; validate utility on target workloads.
usage: Validate synthetic data on your actual workloads; regenerate when workloads change.

demo.code:
print('synthetic: 10k rows, DP eps=1.0')
print('workload queries: within 3% of real-data answers')

title: Signature Local differential privacy
description: Signature edition: In local DP, noise is added on the user's device before data ever leaves — the server never sees raw data. Apple's and Google's telemetry use it: the aggregator learns population statistics while each individual's contribution is deniable. Trust nobody with raw data.
method: Randomize responses client-side (randomized response); aggregate noisy reports; the server only ever sees noise.
usage: Use when users don't trust the collector; expect higher noise (local DP costs more utility).

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(9)
true = 1
reported = true if random.random() < 0.75 else 1 - true  # randomized response
print(f'true {true} -> reported {reported} (plausible deniability)')

title: Signature Composition theorems
description: Signature edition: Running k ε-DP queries gives kε-DP (basic composition); advanced composition and RDP give tighter bounds — the math that makes multi-query analysis affordable. Composition is why the budget accountant can be precise instead of paranoid.
method: Apply basic/advanced/RDP composition to bound total loss; use the tightest applicable theorem; the accountant implements them.
usage: Use RDP accounting in practice; understand which theorem your accountant implements.

demo.code:
print('100 queries, eps=0.1 each: basic -> 10.0; RDP -> 2.3')
print('tighter composition: 4x more queries for the same budget')

title: Signature Privacy-utility tradeoff curves
description: Signature edition: Every ε buys utility and spends privacy; the tradeoff curve plots accuracy vs ε so stakeholders choose deliberately. Publishing the curve — 'at ε=1 we get 92% accuracy, at ε=0.1 we get 78%' — turns the privacy parameter from magic number into business decision.
method: Sweep ε; measure utility; plot the curve; choose ε with stakeholders; document the choice.
usage: Always show the curve; never pick ε by default; revisit as data grows.

demo.code:
curve = [(0.1, 0.78), (0.5, 0.88), (1.0, 0.92), (2.0, 0.94)]
print('eps -> accuracy:', curve)
print('chosen: eps=1.0 (92%) — documented with stakeholders')

title: Signature DP-SGD for private training
description: Signature edition: DP-SGD trains neural networks with differential privacy: clip per-example gradients (bounding sensitivity), add Gaussian noise, and account privacy via the moments accountant. It's how industry trains on sensitive data — the model learns patterns without memorizing individuals.
method: Clip gradients to norm C; add Gaussian noise; update; track (ε,δ) with the moments accountant; stop at budget.
usage: Tune the clipping norm (too small biases, too large wastes budget); track ε throughout training.

demo.code:
print('epoch 10: eps spent 2.1 / 8.0, accuracy 91% (non-private: 94%)')
print('privacy cost of 3 accuracy points: quantified')

title: Signature Privacy budget accounting
description: Signature edition: Every DP query spends privacy budget ε; the accountant tracks total spend and refuses queries that would exceed it. Composition theorems (basic, advanced, RDP) bound the total loss — the budget is the organization's privacy currency, managed like money.
method: Track per-query ε; compose via RDP/moments accountant; halt or require approval when the budget nears exhaustion.
usage: Set budgets per dataset; use RDP accounting for tight bounds; review spend regularly.

title: Signature Exponential mechanism
description: Signature edition: For non-numeric outputs (pick the best category, the median), the exponential mechanism samples outputs with probability proportional to exp(ε·score/2Δ). It brings DP to selections and rankings — choosing privately, not just counting privately.
method: Score each candidate; sample with weight exp(ε·score/2Δ); higher scores more likely; the choice is ε-DP.
usage: Use for private selection; bound the score sensitivity carefully.
